model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between model accuracy (ACC, in percent) and the co-occurrence number, comparing six different methods: Base (black solid line with circular markers), FT (blue solid line with downward triangular markers), IKE (red solid line with upward triangular markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with pentagonal markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 40% to 65%, with major tick marks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, starting at approximately 51% at 10⁰ and rising to about 66% at 10⁴. MEMIT and MEND show moderate performance, beginning near 44% and 45% respectively at 10⁰ and increasing to around 55% and 56% at 10⁴. IKE and FT start near 43% and 40% respectively and rise to approximately 49% and 48% at 10⁴. The Base method remains relatively flat, starting at 38% and reaching only about 44% at 10⁴, indicating minimal improvement with increasing co-occurrence.
